priority: Replace the adjoining coarse source building visible across the lower east facade in candidate 81, using its own complete surveyed envelope.

identification.name: Neutronenleiterhalle Ost
identification.confidence: Probable from its position east of FRM II and public exterior photographs; register the end elevations before assigning openings.

references.credit: MLZ; Reiner Müller / FRM II, TUM
references.use: Exterior material and entrance reference only. No source pixels bundled as textures.
Historical exterior corridor reference only; temporary construction objects are not current architecture.

observations: Public MLZ exterior views show fine horizontal corrugation, silver-grey cladding and a glazed projecting end bay above a large loading opening.
The historical corridor photograph shows the side facing the reactor: grey corrugated metal, a continuous narrow glazed band and additional taller glazed strips.
The survey resolves two elevated end projections and four low roof volumes; retain their measured geometry instead of copying the neighboring reactor panel grid.
limitations: Assign each photograph to a surveyed elevation before drawing its openings.
Corrugation pitch, frame sizes and loading-opening dimensions require explicit estimates.
No interiors or plant equipment are in scope.
The implementation uses inferred matching glazing on both stepped end projections; detailed end registration remains unresolved.
nextActions: Register the observed end and corridor elevations to the 44 survey walls.
Reconstruct the complete measured envelope with qualified corrugated materials and photographed window groups; keep exact roof geometry.
Extend source retirement only where the new envelope replaces it, preserving the reconstructed FRM II body and other neighbors.
Compare the retained east camera and add exterior ground approaches with adequate measured terrain.
